en.title: Australian High Commissioner to Maldives calls on Minister Shahid
en.description: Australian High Commissioner to Maldives calls on Minister Shahid
en.body:
Australian High Commissioner to Maldives calls on Minister Shahid

The first Resident High Commissioner of Australia to Maldives, David Jessup, paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid today. The meeting took place following the presentation of his Credentials to His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of Maldives, earlier in the day.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid extended warm congratulations to the Australian High Commissioner and thanked Australia for its decision to establish a resident mission in the Maldives. Australian High Commissioner conveyed his gratitude for the warm welcome extended to him and mentioned it was a privilege for him to take up the responsibility of representing the Government of Australia in the Maldives.

Highlighting the remarkable growth and expansion of the Australia-Maldives partnership over the years, the High Commissioner emphasized its positive impact in various areas, including climate change, security cooperation, and human resource development. High Commissioner Jessup was accompanied by Deputy High Commissioner Andrew Hodges.

Minister Shahid was joined by State Minister Ahmed Khaleel, Secretary-Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, and Director Adam Hamid.

en.title: The Maldives submits a written statement to the ICJ with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem
en.description: The Maldives submits a written statement to the ICJ with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the occupied Palestinian Territory…
en.body:
The Maldives submits a written statement to the ICJ with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem

The Maldives has submitted a written statement to the International Court of Justice with regard to the request for an Advisory Opinion on the legal consequences arising from the policies and practises of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem.  
  
The request for an Advisory Opinion was made through resolution 77/247, which was passed during the 77th session of the United Nations General Assembly. The Maldives voted in favour of the resolution.

The statement was prepared by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Attorney General’s Office.

The Maldives has always stood in solidarity with the Palestinian people in their fight for self-determination and the realisation of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine established on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

THE END

en.title: Secretary (West) of the Ministry of External Affairs of India calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Secretary (West) of the Ministry of External Affairs of India calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
Secretary (West) of the Ministry of External Affairs of India calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs

Secretary (West) of the Ministry of External Affairs of India, Sanjay Verma, called on the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, today. The meeting was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid emphasised on the importance of solidifying joint efforts in addressing the common security challenges to ensure peace and stability in both countries and the Indian Ocean region. Reflecting on the second meeting of India-Maldives joint working group on counter-terrorism, countering violent extremism and de-radicalisation held yesterday, both Minister Shahid and Secretary Verma reviewed the significant initiatives undertaken by both Maldives and India. They also discussed on further avenues to consolidate the ties of two countries in this area bilaterally and in the multilateral arena.

Secretary Verma is on a three-day Official Visit to the Maldives to co-chair the second meeting of India-Maldives joint working group on counter-terrorism, countering violent extremism and de-radicalisation.

ENDS

en.title: The newly appointed Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to the Maldives calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: The newly appointed Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to the Maldives calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
The newly appointed Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to the Maldives calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs

The newly appointed Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to the Maldives, Sheikh Rahma bin Abdulrahman bin Rahma Al Shamsi paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs this afternoon, Minister Shahid welcomed the Ambassador to the Maldives and congratulated him on presenting his credentials as the Ambassador of the UAE to the Maldives.

Minister also expressed hope that the long-standing, close relations between the Maldives and the UAE will be further strengthened during the Ambassador’s term. Minister Shahid and the UAE Ambassador discussed prospects for further diversifying the partnership between the Maldives and the UAE. The Ambassador assured the commitment of the Government of UAE to advance the shared priorities and interests with the Maldives.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel; Secretary, Bilateral, Dr. Hala Hameed; Joint Secretary, Mariyam Reesha; Director, Ahmed Fazeel; and Assistant Director, Mohamed Shahudhan Shaheem.

en.title: Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt, Ambassador Ayman Kamel, pays a courtesy call on Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid
en.description: Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt, Ambassador Ayman Kamel, pays a courtesy call on Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid
en.body:
Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt, Ambassador Ayman Kamel, pays a courtesy call on Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid

The Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Arab Republic of Egypt, Ambassador Ayman Kamel, paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid today.

At the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid welcomed the Assistant Minister and his delegation to the Maldives and reaffirmed the strong commitment of the Government of Maldives to further enhance bilateral cooperation with Egypt and increase collaboration at the international fora on matters of mutual interest. Minister Shahid conveyed appreciation to the leadership and the Government of Egypt for the continuous assistance and opportunities granted to the Maldives over the years, which stands as a testament to the close relations between the two countries. Minister Shahid also conveyed the commitment of the Maldives to implement the outcomes agreed upon by the two countries during the Bilateral Political Consultations held in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 16 July 2023.

The Assistant Minister of Egypt assured the unwavering support of the Government of Egypt to the Maldives, to advance shared priorities and interests and to collaborate on strengthening bilateral and multilateral relations.

The Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Egypt, Ambassador Ayman Kamel is on an official visit to the Maldives, to attend the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations between the Maldives and Egypt held on 16 July 2023. Ambassador Kamel was accompanied by the Ambassador of the Arab Republic of Egypt to the Republic of Maldives, Maged Mosleh Nafei.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel; Secretary, Bilateral, Dr. Hala Hameed; Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Maldives to the Arab Republic of Egypt, Aminath Shabeena; Joint Secretary, Mariyam Reesha; and Director, Ahmed Fazeel.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
en.description: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives His Excellency Abdulla Shahid sent a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea His Excellency Park Jin, following the torrential rain which caused widespread damage in the Republic of Korea.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"I am deeply saddened to hear the news of the loss of lives and damage to thousands of households and property, caused by the devastating landslides and flooding that has resulted from the torrential rains across the Republic of Korea.

The Government and the people of Maldives join me in conveying our heartfelt condolences to the families and friends who lost their loved ones.

I sincerely hope that the efforts of the response teams continue swiftly and successfully. Wishing for a quick recovery for those injured."

en.title: Maldives Delegation actively participated in the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: Maldives Delegation actively participated in the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council
en.body:
Maldives Delegation actively participated in the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council

The 53rd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council concluded in Geneva on Friday.

The Human Rights Council adopted 31 resolutions and the Delegation of Maldives delivered 32 national statements on an array of thematic areas. The Maldives co-sponsored 14 resolutions, including the Enhancement of international cooperation in the field of human rights, Contribution of development to the enjoyment of all human rights, Negative impact of corruption on the enjoyment of human rights and the mandate renewal of the Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities among others.

The Maldives was part of the cross-regional core group that drafted the resolution on the Mandate of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers. The main objective of this resolution is to renew the mandate of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers for a further period of three years. This resolution was adopted by consensus and had more than 71 co-sponsors supporting the resolution at the time of adoption. Further, in response to a request by the Organization for Islamic Cooperation (OIC), an urgent debate was held on 11th July with the purpose of bringing attention to the recent attacks on the sanctity of Holy Quran. The Maldives was a proud co-sponsor of the resolution titled “Countering religious hatred constituting incitement to discrimination, hostility or violence.” This resolution, adopted after the urgent debate at the 53rd Session, vehemently condemns the desecration of the Holy Quran.

The Maldives also co-sponsored 34 joint statements delivered at the Council. This included statements by the Organization for Islamic Cooperation among others. The Maldives on behalf of the group of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) delivered a statement at the Annual Panel Discussion on the theme of Adverse Impacts of Climate Change on the full realization of the right to food and reiterated SIDS commitment to work collectively to build resilient food systems that safeguard the right to food to ensure a sustainable future for all.

The Maldives Delegation at the 53rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council was led by H.E. Dr. Asim Ahmed, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary and Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Office at Geneva. As the Vice President of the Council, representing the Asia Pacific Group, Dr. Asim Ahmed chaired several meetings of the Council.

en.title: The Maldives and Egypt to hold the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations
en.description: The Maldives and Egypt to hold the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations
en.body:
The Maldives and Egypt to hold the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations

The Maldives and Egypt will hold the Second Round of Bilateral Political Consultations on 16 July 2023 in Male’.

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel will lead the Political Consultations on behalf of the Government of Maldives. His Excellency Ambassador Ayman Kamel, Assistant Minister for Asian Affairs of the Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Egypt will co-chair the Political Consultations on behalf of the Government of Egypt.

During the Consultations, Maldives and Egypt will discuss bilateral and multilateral issues of mutual concern.

The First Round of Bilateral Political Consultations between the Maldives and Egypt was held in Cairo, Egypt on 19 December 2019.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to Iraq
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to Iraq
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Republic Day greetings to Iraq

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations to Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Iraq, Fuad Mohammad Hussein, on the occasion of Iraq’s Republic Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Iraq, on the auspicious occasion of your Republic Day.

It is my earnest hope that the friendship between our two countries will continue to grow even stronger in the years ahead.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to France
en.description: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to France
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to France

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of greetings to Catherine Colonna, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of the French Republic, on the festive occasion of the National Day of France.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives, I am delighted to extend warm wishes to Your Excellency, the People and the Government of the French Republic on the joyous occasion of the National Day of France on the 14th of July.

The Maldives values the enduring friendship and collaborative partnership we share with France, spanning over 54 years of diplomatic relations. We look forward to strengthening our ties even further as we address present challenges and embrace future opportunities together.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration as well as sincere wishes for your continued good health and the everlasting prosperity of your great country.”

dv.title: މިސްރަށް ދާ ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލްގެ ދަށުން ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެ އިންތިޒާމު ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ
dv.description: މިސްރަށް ދާ ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލްގެ ދަށުން ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެ އިންތިޒާމު ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ
dv.body:
މިސްރަށް ދާ ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލްގެ ދަށުން ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެ އިންތިޒާމު ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން މިޞްރަށް ދަތުރުކުރާ ދިވެހިންނަށް ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލް (އިމަޖެންސީ އެންޓްރީ ވިސާ) ގެ ދަށުން ދަތުރުކުރެވޭނެ އިންތިޒާމް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެއެވެ. މި އިންތިޒާމުގެދަށުން، ދިވެހި ޕާސްޕޯޓް (އޯޑިނަރީ، ޑިޕްލޮމެޓިކް އަދި އޮފިޝަލް ޕާސްޕޯޓް) އޮންނަ ފަރާތްތަކުން މިޞްރަށް ދަތުރުކޮށް އެ ޤައުމަށް އެތެރެވާ ދުވަހުން ފެށިގެން ގިނަވެގެން 30 ދުވަހުގެ މުއްދަތަކަށް އެ ޤައުމުގައި ތިބެވޭނެއެވެ. މި ވިސާއަކީ ޓޫރިސްޓް ވިސާއެކެވެ. އަދި މި ވިސާގެ ފީއަކީ 25 ޑޮލަރެވެ.

ދިވެހި ޕާސްޕޯޓް އޮންނަ ފަރާތްތަކަށް ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލް ދިނުމަށް މިޞްރު ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމާފައިވީ ނަމަވެސް، 30 ދުވަހަށްވުރެ ދިގު މުއްދަތަކަށް މިޞްރަށް ޒިޔާރަތްކުރާ ނުވަތަ ވަޒީފާ އަދާކުރުމަށް ނުވަތަ ތަޢުލީމް ޙާޞިލްކުރުމަށް ނުވަތަ މިޞްރުގައި ވިޔަފާރިކުރުމަށް ބޭނުންވާ ދިވެހިން މިޞްރަށް ދަތުރުކުމުގެކުރިން އެކަމަކާގުޅޭ ވިސާއެއް ނަގަންޖެހޭނެއެވެ.

ދިވެހިންނަށް މިޞްރަށް ވިސާ އޮން އެރައިވަލް ދިނުމަށް މިޞްރު ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމި މި މުހިންމު ނިންމުން، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ދެކެނީ ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އޮތް ގާތް ރަޙުމަތްތެރި ގުޅުމާއި މިޞްރުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ދޭ ޚާއްޞަ އަހައްމިއްޔަތުކަމުގެ ރަމްޒެއްގެ ގޮތުގައެވެ

en.title: Minister Shahid extends Statehood Day greetings to Montenegro
en.description: Minister Shahid extends Statehood Day greetings to Montenegro
en.body:
Minister Shahid extends Statehood Day greetings to Montenegro

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, sends a message of congratulations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro, Ranko Krivokapić on the occasion of the Statehood Day of Montenegro.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"It is with great pleasure that I extend warm greetings and best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Montenegro on the joyous occasion of Statehood Day.

I am confident that the close ties of friendship between our countries will continue to flourish, paving the way for enhanced collaboration in various spheres in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes and the assurances of my highest consideration."

en.title: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets with Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s First Assistant Secretary
en.description: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets with Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s First Assistant Secretary
en.body:
State Minister Ahmed Khaleel meets with Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s First Assistant Secretary

The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel met with Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s First Assistant Secretary for North and South Asia Division Gary Cowan, today. During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, both State Minister Khaleel and First Assistant Secretary Cowan reviewed the strong bilateral cooperation between the two countries across a multitude of areas including human resource development, human rights, democracy and the rule of law, and security cooperation.

State Minister Khaleel and First Assistant Secretary Cowan also reflected on the enhanced bilateral relations between the two countries in the recent years, especially with the opening of the Australian High Commission in Malé.

Discussions also focused on the cordial ties in the multilateral arena on issues of mutual interest. State Minister Khaleel and First Assistant Secretary Cowan further emphasised the strong commitment of both sides, on advancing peace and security in the Indo-Pacific region.

As First Assistant Secretary Cowan’s visit coincides with the farewell of the Australian High Commissioner to the Maldives Paul Stephens, State Minister Khaleel extended his gratitude to the High Commissioner and the team in the Australian High Commission in Colombo for their work over the years towards strengthening the relations between Maldives and Australia.

First Assistant Secretary Gary Cowan was accompanied by Australian High Commissioner to the Maldives Paul Stephens, Deputy High Commissioner Andrew Hodges, Second Secretary Lara Sveinsson and Policy Officer Nikola Damjanovski.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, and Desk Officer Saifulla Waleed.

en.title: Minister Shahid, departs after concluding his Official Visit to India
en.description: Minister Shahid, departs after concluding his Official Visit to India
en.body:
Minister Shahid, departs after concluding his Official Visit to India

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid departed India after concluding his Official Visit to New Delhi.

During the visit, Minister of Foreign Affairs met with the Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar. Bilateral talks were also held between both countries where in-depth discussion on all aspects of the relations between the Maldives and India took place. The historic relationship between both countries were reflected and commitments were exchanged to continue working closely together, bilaterally and in the international fora, on priority areas of mutual interest. Both Ministers shared their visions relating to development cooperation, tourism cooperation, human resource development, multilateral engagements, and consular affairs. Both Minister Shahid and Minister Dr. Jaishankar also emphasized on the importance of exploring further avenues to deepen the Maldives-India partnership.

During his visit, Minister Shahid also presided the exchange of nine Memorandum of Understandings between Maldives and India in the field of socio-economic development, along with the Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar.

Additionally, Minister Shahid delivered the 43rd Sapru House Lecture (SHL) at the Indian Council of World Affairs. In the lecture titled “The Power of Small: The Maldives Story”, Minister Shahid outlined how Maldives as a small State navigated the perils of international diplomacy through adapting and adjusting by means of successful strategies.

In addition, Minister Shahid also met with the Non-Resident High Commissioners and Ambassadors accredited to the Maldives based in New Delhi, at the reception hosted by the High Commissioner of Maldives to India, in honour of Minister Shahid. Minister Shahid also visited the High Commission of Maldives in India where he met with the diplomatic and local staff. Minister also engaged with several Indian media and spoke about the Maldives-India partnership, the overall development of Maldives and India’s pivotal role.

Minister Shahid was seen off at the Indhira Gandhi International Airport by the High Commissioner of Maldives to India, Ibrahim Shaheeb and Mr. Puneet Agarwal, Joint Secretary, IOR of the Ministry of External Affairs of India.

en.title: Visa on arrival for Maldivians travelling to Egypt
en.description: Visa on arrival for Maldivians travelling to Egypt
en.body:
Visa on arrival for Maldivians travelling to Egypt

The Arab Republic of Egypt has made the decision to grant visa on arrival (emergency entry visa) to Maldivian nationals travelling to Egypt. The on arrival tourist visa allows all Maldivian passport holders (Ordinary, Diplomatic and Official) to enter and stay in Egypt for a maximum period of thirty (30) days from the day of their entry, with a visa fee of USD 25.

Maldivians intending to stay for a longer period or wishing to travel to Egypt for work or to attend an educational institution or to conduct business in the Arab Republic of Egypt, will need to obtain an appropriate visa prior to their travel.

The Government of Maldives considers this momentous decision by the Government of Egypt as a testament to the close and historic relations between the two countries and the high regard accorded to the Maldives by the Arab Republic of Egypt.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Minister of External Affairs of India
en.description: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Minister of External Affairs of India
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Minister of External Affairs of India

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of sympathy and condolence ‎‎to the Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar, following the loss of lives and livelihoods caused by the widespread floods and devastating landslides in the northern States of India. Minister’s message reads as follows:

“I am greatly saddened to hear the news of the widespread floods and devastating landslides caused by torrential rains in the northern States of India, leading to loss of lives, destroying livelihoods and infrastructure, and displacement of people.

At this time of distress, on behalf of the Government and the people of Maldives, I extend deepest sympathies and condolences to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of India. I extend our heartfelt prayers to alleviate the sufferings to those effected, especially to the bereaved families.

I hope that the rescue and recovery efforts proceed swiftly with ease. I praise and pray for the perseverance of the people of India during this difficult time.”

en.title: Minister Shahid visits the High Commission of Maldives in India
en.description: Minister Shahid visits the High Commission of Maldives in India
en.body:
Minister Shahid visits the High Commission of Maldives in India

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid paid a visit to the Chancery building of the High Commission of the Republic of Maldives in New Delhi, this morning.

On arrival to the Chancery, Minister Shahid was welcomed by High Commissioner of Maldives to India, Ibrahim Shaheeb. During the visit Minister Shahid met the staff and took stock of the work carried out by the Mission. Minister Shahid expressed appreciation for the contribution by staff towards strengthening bilateral partnership between Maldives and India. Following the meeting Minister Shahid toured the premises.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral, Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Abdul Waris Saeed, and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Minister Shahid is on an Official Visit to India.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to São Tomé and Príncipe
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to São Tomé and Príncipe
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to São Tomé and Príncipe

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Communities of the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe, Alberto Neto Pereira, on the occasion of São Tomé and Príncipe’s Independence Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of São Tomé and Príncipe, on the joyous occasion of your Independence Day.

With the formal establishment of diplomatic relations between our two countries last year, I look forward to increased bilateral engagements between our two countries in the years ahead.

Let me also convey my earnest hopes for continued peace, progress and prosperity for the friendly people of São Tomé and Príncipe.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with Non-Resident High Commissioners and Ambassadors accredited to the Maldives based in New Delhi
en.description: Minister Shahid meets with Non-Resident High Commissioners and Ambassadors accredited to the Maldives based in New Delhi
en.body:
Minister Shahid meets with Non-Resident High Commissioners and Ambassadors accredited to the Maldives based in New Delhi

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with Non-Resident High Commissioners and Ambassadors accredited to the Maldives based in New Delhi. The interaction took place at the reception hosted by the High Commissioner of Maldives to India, Ibrahim Shaheeb, in honour of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid.

Speaking at the reception, Minister Shahid delivered a remark in which he highlighted that the countries represented at the reception were valuable bilateral and multilateral partners to the Maldives. He also emphasized that bilateral relationship is the cornerstone of all international relations, and as accredited Ambassadors and High Commissioners, the Envoys had a heavy responsibility for strengthening and sustaining the relationship. Minister Shahid also underscored that people to people connections are crucial to bridge the gap and nurture closer cooperation between the countries.

Highlighting the upcoming candidatures of Maldives for the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) and the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), Minister Shahid noted that the Maldives relied on the power of diplomacy and international cooperation, based on the three pillars of the its foreign policy, namely the promotion and protection of human rights, consolidating democracy, and championing climate diplomacy. He also added that the Maldives intends to meaningfully contribute towards maintaining international peace and security at the Security Council, and push for enhanced coordination and coherence across the UN system to help all countries achieve the SDGs and all its targets at the ECOSOC.

The reception hosted at Taj Palace, New Delhi was attended by Envoys from Algeria, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Bulgaria, Chile, Colombia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Eritrea, Finland, Gambia, Georgia, Ghana, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Kenya, Laos, Mauritius, Mexico, Morocco, Namibia, Oman, Peru, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Guinea, Republic of Sudan, Rwanda, Senegal Serbia, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Uganda, Ukraine and Zimbabwe.

Minister Abdulla Shahid is on an Official Visit to India.

en.title: Minister Shahid speaks on the Maldives journey in establishing itself in the international arena, through its vulnerabilities and challenges at the Indian Council for World Affairs
en.description: Minister Shahid speaks at the Indian Council of World Affairs
en.body:
Minister Shahid speaks at the Indian Council of World Affairs

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, outlined how Maldives, as small State navigated the perils of international diplomacy through adapting and adjusting by means of successful strategies, while delivering the 43rd Sapru House Lecture at the Indian Council of World Affairs, on the topic “The Power of Small: The Maldives Story”, today in New Delhi.

Minister Shahid spoke in detail about the pressing challenges faced by Small Island States like the Maldives in getting the opportunity to serve in significant roles at the multilateral arena. He reflected on the sentiment which arose when Maldives applied for membership of the United Nations with questioning about the ability to undertake the responsibilities of a responsible member of the international community and the capacity to engage constructively. Minister Shahid emphasized that the principles enshrined in the United Nations Charter offered the small States an equal footing in multilateralism.

Minister Shahid also highlighted how Maldives began implementing an independent foreign policy immediately after signing independence in 1965; and how the Maldives adopted key strategies to adapt to the circumstances. He focused on the three approaches adopted by the Maldives, namely the “principled”, “pragmatic” and the “prioritization” approach which demonstrated how a small State can defend itself and their interests, and defend others infront of bigger States in global settings.

The 43rd Sapru House Lecture was introduced and moderated by Director General of the Indian Council of World Affairs, Ambassador Vijay Thakur Singh. The Indian Council for World Affairs is an Indian think tank that was established in 1943.

en.title: Ceremony held to exchange Memorandums of Understanding between Maldives and India

Ceremony held to exchange Memorandums of Understanding between Maldives and India

A number of significant Memorandums of Understanding were exchanged between Maldives and India in various fields, expanding the cooperation between two countries at a ceremony held today in New Delhi, India. The ceremony was presided by Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid and the Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar.

At today’s ceremony, High Commissioner of Maldives to India, Ibrahim Shaheeb and High Commissioner of India to the Maldives, Munu Mahawar exchanged nine Memorandums of Understanding between the Government of Maldives and the Government of India to implement socio-economic development projects throughout the Maldives under the High Impact Community Development Project scheme grant funding from the Government of India. These projects include the Development of Mental Health Unit at R. Ungoofaaru Hospital, Development of Volley Court in Sh. Kanditheemu, Establishment of Geydhoshu Mas Plant in M. Dhiggaru, Procurement of Furniture and Equipment for Sh. Foakaidhoo Community Centre, School Digitalization Project in Th. Vilufushi, Upgrading F. Nilandhoo Hospital, Upgrading School Computer Lab, Utheemu Palace Roof Preservation and Development of Palace Surroundings Project and Installation of Street Lights in Ga. Kondey.

The ceremony was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives and the Ministry of External Affairs of India.

en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid and Minister of External Affairs, Dr. S. Jaishankar hold official discussions

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid held bilateral talks with Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar today. Both sides had an in-depth discussion on all aspects of the relations between the Maldives and India. They reflected on the historic relationship between both countries and expressed commitment to continue working closely together, bilaterally and in the international fora, on priority areas of mutual interest.

During the official discussion held at Hyderabad House in New Delhi, both Ministers noted the successful economic cooperation and the progress of projects that is being implemented under Indian grant assistance and line of credit schemes. Both Ministers exchanged views and shared their visions relating to development cooperation, tourism cooperation, human resource development, multilateral engagements, and consular affairs between both countries. Both Minister Shahid and Minister Dr. Jaishankar also emphasized on the importance of exploring further avenues to deepen the Maldives-India partnership.

Minister Shahid expressed gratitude to the Government of India for the constant support to facilitate and further develop economic, trade and investment ties between both countries, and for India’s commitment in the socioeconomic development of the Maldives.

The Maldives and Azerbaijan signs MoU on increasing cooperation between the two foreign ministries

The Maldives and Azerbaijan have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on increasing cooperation between the Ministries of Foreign Affairs of both countries. The MoU was signed today at a ceremony held on the sidelines of the Ministerial Meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) that is presently ongoing in Baku, Azerbaijan.

The MoU aims to enhance and expand bilateral relations and cooperation between the Maldives and Azerbaijan, and also facilitate the holding of regular consultations between the two countries at all levels on issues of mutual interest. It also aims to strengthen cooperation between the two sides on the training of diplomats.

The MoU was signed by His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, on behalf of the Government of Maldives, and His Excellency Elnur Mammadov, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, on behalf of the Government of Azerbaijan.

en.title: Maldives calls on the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) to address emerging challenges of the day
en.description: Maldives calls on the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) to address emerging challenges of the day
en.body:
Maldives calls on the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) to address emerging challenges of the day

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, today delivered remarks during the Ministerial Meeting of the Coordinating Bureau of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) in Baku, Azerbaijan.

State Minister Khaleel commended Azerbaijan’s strong commitment and efforts as the outgoing Chair of NAM, which was crucial for the accomplishments of NAM, especially during the height of the pandemic. He then welcomed Uganda as the next chair of NAM and expressed confidence in their leadership and ability to steer the work of NAM.

Acknowledging the important role NAM can continue to play in achieving prosperity and peace, he stressed the need to further strengthen cooperation and collaboration to address shared challenges, such as climate change and food security – challenges Small Island Developing States like Maldives are particularly vulnerable to.

The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), created in 1961, is a grouping of 120 countries that are not aligned with, or against any major power blocs. Following the end of the Cold War in 1991, it has broadened its mandate to focus on emerging non-traditional challenges. The Maldives became a member of this organization in 1976.

dv.body:
އަޟްޙާ ޢީދު ދުވަހާ ދިމާކޮށް ސްވިޑެންގައި މުޞްޙަފް އެންދުމާއިގުޅިގެން މިކަން އިތުރަށް ތަކުރާރު ވިޔަނުދިނުމަށްޓަކައި އެޅިދާނެ ފިޔަވަޅުތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރުމަށްޓަކައި އޯ.އައި.ސީ. ގެ މައި މަރުކަޒުގައި މިއަދު ބޭއްވި އެ ޖަމުއިއްޔާގެ އެގްޒެކެޓިވް ކޮމިޓީގެ އޯޕަން-އެންޑެޑް ކުއްލި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފަރާތުން އޯ.އައި.ސީ. އަށް ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބު އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފަރާތުން ސައުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާއަށް ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު އަލްފާޟިލް މުޙައްމަދު ޚަލީލް ބައިވެރިވެ ވަޑައިގަތެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ސްވިޑެންގައި މުޞްޙަފް އެންދި މައްސަލައާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން އެ މަނިކުފާނު ވަނީ ތަޤްރީރު ކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ ތަޤްރީރުގައި އަޟްޙާ ޢީދު ދުވަހާ ދިމާކޮށް ސްވިޑެންގައި މުޞްޙަފް އަންދައި ހިންގައިފައިވާ މި ހަޑިހުތުރު އަމަލު ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ހަރުކަށި އިބާރާތުން ކުށްވެރިކުރައްވާކަން ހާމަކުރެއްވިއެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން މިފަދަ އިޙްތިރާމް ކުޑަ ޢަމަލު ތަކުރާރުވުމަކީވެސް މުޅި ދުނިޔޭގެ އެތައް މިލިއަން މުސްލިމުންގެ ދީނީ ޝުޢޫރުތަކަށް އަނިޔާވާ ކަމެއް ކަމަށާއި، ހަމައެކަނި ޚިޔާލުފާޅުކުރުމުގެ މިނިވަންކަމުގެ މައްޗަށް ބިނާކޮށް މިފަދަ އަމަލުތައް ހިންގުމަށް ހުއްދަ ދިނުމަކީ ބަލައިނުގަނެވޭނެ ކަމެއްކަމުގައި ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި އިސްލާމްދީނާ ދެކޮޅަށް ހިންގާ މިފަދަ ނަފްރަތު އުފެދޭ އަމަލުތައް ނިމުމަކަށް ގެނައުމަށްވެސް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ތަކުރާރުކޮށް ގޮވާލަމުންދާކަން ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Canada Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Canada
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Canada Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Canada

Minister Shahid sends Canada Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Canada

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends message of felicitations to Melanie Joly, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada, on the occasion of Canada Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and sincere good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the friendly people of Canada, on the occasion of Canada Day.

Throughout our more than four-decade-long bilateral relations, Canada has remained a reliable ally to the Maldivian people, especially in times of crises. The Maldives highly values its close relationship with Canada. I am confident that this partnership will continue to expand.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress and prosperity for the people of Canada and the assurances of my highest considerations.”

en.title: Minister Shahid calls on all States to uphold their commitments, to ensure effective implementation of the "High Seas Treaty."
en.description: Minister Shahid calls on all States to uphold their commitments, to ensure effective implementation of the "High Seas Treaty."
en.body:
Minister Shahid calls on all States to uphold their commitments, to ensure effective implementation of the "High Seas Treaty."

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, delivered a statement today in the Further Resumed Session of the Fifth Session of Intergovernmental Consultations (IGC) on an Internationally legally binding instrument under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction, in New York. The “BBNJ Treaty”, also known as the “Treaty of the High Seas” was adopted at this session.

Minister Shahid emphasized the significance of such a treaty in his statement, noting that it provides a framework for operationalising the equity principles of the United Nations Law of the Sea Convention into practice. He noted that this instrument would significantly lessen the conservation-related burden on Small Island Developing States and help reduce ocean regime inequity, particularly in areas of marine scientific research and sharing of benefits from utilizing marine genetic resources in Areas Beyond National Jurisdictions. And pointed out that this is particularly crucial for nations like the Maldives, which are in the forefront of the climate emergency while simultaneously being the custodians of huge oceanic expanses and with limited resources. Consequently, Minister Shahid urged all States to uphold their commitments and work collectively towards effective implementation of the High Seas Treaty.

The Intergovernmental Conference on Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction is held under the auspices of the United Nations, to consider the recommendations of the Preparatory Committee established by resolution 69/292 of 19 June 2015 on the elements and to elaborate the text of an international legally binding instrument under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity of areas beyond national jurisdiction.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“Your Excellency,

I was shocked and deeply saddened to hear the news about the horrific attack on Lhubiria Secondary School in Mpondwe yesterday that has claimed the lives of many students and caused injury to others.

The Government of Maldives condemns this heinous act of terror in the strongest of terms. The Government and the people of the Maldives join me in extending our deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathies to the Government and people of Uganda, in particular, to the families of the deceased and injured in yesterday’s attack.”

en.title: Maldives to Participate in the 53rd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council
en.description: The 53rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council began today in Geneva, Switzerland. The session will be held from 19 June 2023 to 14 July 2023.
en.body:
The 53rd Session of the UN Human Rights Council began today in Geneva, Switzerland. The session will be held from 19 June 2023 to 14 July 2023.

During the Session, the Maldives delegation will deliver national statements under several agenda items, in line with the Government’s key policies and priorities. The Maldives will also be delivering a joint statement for the Annual Panel on Adverse Impacts of Climate Change on behalf of a group of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) based in Geneva.

Additionally, the Maldives, together with a cross regional core group, will present a resolution extending the mandate of Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers.

The Maldives delegation for the 53rd Session of the Human Rights Council is led by His Excellency Dr. Asim Ahmed, Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices at Geneva. The delegation includes Ms. Hawla Ahmed Didi, Deputy Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Mr. Hassan Hussain Shihab, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, Counsellor of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva, Ms. Maryam Fathika Fayaz, Second Secretary of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva and Ms. Nafha Hassan, Third Secretary of the Maldives Mission to the United Nations Offices at Geneva.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with the United Nations Secretary-General
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid met with the Secretary-General of the United Nations, António Guterres in New York today.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid met with the Secretary-General of the United Nations, António Guterres in New York today.

At the meeting held during the Minister’s official visit to Washington D.C. and New York, Minister Shahid reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Maldives to the United Nations and its Charter, and its commitment to working on priorities such as climate change, environmental sustainability, gender equality and youth empowerment.

Minister Shahid thanked the Secretary-General for including the Maldives as one of the 30 pilot countries for the “Early Warnings for All” Initiative. He also commended the Secretary-General on his decision to convene a “Climate Ambition Summit” during the High-Level Week of the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, and in this context, noted the work that needs to be done ahead of COP28 to the UNFCCC, to be held in the United Arab Emirates later in the year.

The Minister also heard a briefing from the Secretary General on the ongoing issues of concern at the United Nations. He committed the full support of the Maldivian delegation to the Secretary General, and his team.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid was accompanied by State Minister Khaleel, Secretary, Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed and Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations, Thilmeeza Hussain.

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid pays a courtesy call on the President of Seychelles
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid paid a courtesy call on the President of Seychelles, Wavel Ramkalawan today, during the President’s State Visit to the Maldives.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid paid a courtesy call on the President of Seychelles, Wavel Ramkalawan today, during the President’s State Visit to the Maldives.

At the meeting held at Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi, Minister Shahid welcomed the President and his delegation to the Maldives and reaffirmed the strong commitment of the Government of Maldives to further enhance bilateral cooperation and increase collaboration at the regional and international levels on matters of mutual interest.

Minister Shahid further noted that the agreements signed today, will be mutually beneficial to both, the people of Maldives and the people Seychelles and expressed hope that the Visa Exemption Agreement will allow greater people-to-people interaction between both countries. Minister Shahid also reaffirmed that the Maldives stands ready to implement the outcomes agreed upon by the two leaders during the Official Talks held in the morning at the President’s Office.

President Wavel Ramkalawan is currently on a State Visit to the Maldives from 11 – 14 June 2023 on the invitation of the President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. President Ramkalawan is accompanied by Her Excellency Linda Ramkalawan, First Lady of the Republic of Seychelles and a high-level delegation from the Government of Seychelles, including His Excellency Sylvestre Radegonde, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Tourism

en.title: Minister Shahid hosts Reception to mark the re-opening of the Embassy of Maldives in the United States
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid hosted a reception to mark the re-opening of the Embassy of the Maldives to United States today. Minister Shahid officially opened the Embassy in a ribbon…
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid hosted a reception to mark the re-opening of the Embassy of the Maldives to United States today. Minister Shahid officially opened the Embassy in a ribbon cutting ceremony on 15 June 2023, marking a return to a full-time diplomatic presence after 14 years.

The reception to mark the re-opening today was attended by Chief Justice of the Maldives, Uz. Ahmed Muthasim Adnan, Assistant Secretary of State, Donald Lu and other senior Government Officials from the White House, State Department, Treasury, USAID, Office of the United States Trade Representative, United States Chamber of Commerce, think tanks and media, and audience from wider diplomatic community. This ceremony was also attended by the resident Maldivian community in Washington, D.C.

The Embassy of the Maldives to the United States will serve as a vital bridge between the two countries in cultivating economic growth, cultural and people-to-people ties that will mutually benefit both nations. The establishment of the Embassy signals a bold new era of reinvigorated and strengthened diplomatic ties between the Maldives and the United States, and will no doubt bring forth greater cooperation and collaboration between the two countries in the global arena.

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with Mr. Jon Finer, Deputy National Security Advisor

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with USAID Administrator Samantha Power

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with the United States Secretary of State Antony Blinken
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid met the Secretary of State of the United States of America Antony Blinken, today marking a pivotal moment in the bilateral relationship between the two countries. The meeting…
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid met the Secretary of State of the United States of America Antony Blinken, today marking a pivotal moment in the bilateral relationship between the two countries. The meeting took place at a crucial juncture as both Maldives and United States establishes resident embassies in their respective capitals, underscoring the commitment to revitalize friendship and cooperation.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid met the Secretary of State of the United States of America Antony Blinken, today marking a pivotal moment in the bilateral relationship between the two countries. The meeting took place at a crucial juncture as both Maldives and United States establishes resident embassies in their respective capitals, underscoring the commitment to revitalize friendship and cooperation.

The discussions between Minister Shahid and Secretary Blinken centered on a range of issues, including promoting and strengthening democracy, commitment to economic growth, adapting to a changing climate, defence cooperation, free and fair elections and freedom of expression and association.

The Maldives and United States acknowledged the importance of upholding a rules-based international order and expressed their commitment to regional stability, maritime security, and promoting peace. Minister Shahid reaffirmed the Maldives' dedication to maintaining peace and security in the Indo-Pacific, while also expressing appreciation for the United States' engagement in the region.

Secretary Blinken congratulated the Maldives on the successful efforts to consolidate democracy. He further acknowledged Maldives’ leadership in climate diplomacy to ensure increased global commitment to combat climate change and promote environmental sustainability.

During the meeting Minister Shahid requested for increased higher education opportunities for Maldivians to study at American universities, highlighting the importance of academic exchanges, scholarships, and collaboration across various fields of study.

Furthermore, Minister Shahid also emphasized the importance of waiving of visas for Maldivians traveling to the United States, aiming to promote people-to-people contact. Secretary Blinken acknowledged the importance of enhancing such contact and assured Minister Shahid that the United States would explore possibilities to streamline visa procedures for Maldivian nationals. This would promote greater cultural exchange, tourism, and business ties, further strengthening the bonds between the two nations.

Minister Shahid was accompanied at the meeting by State Minister Ahmed Khaleel, Ambassador of the Maldives to the United States of America Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, Permanent Representative of Maldives to the United Nations Thilmeeza Hussain, Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Chief of Protocol Ahmed Shiaan, Director General Ahmed Nasir and Counsellor at the Maldives Embassy Zeena Didi.

en.title: The New Ambassador of Maldives to Bhutan Presents Credentials to the King of Bhutan
en.description: The New Non-Resident Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the Kingdom of Bhutan, His Excellency Ibrahim Shaheeb, presented his Letter of Credence to the King of Bhutan, His Majesty Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck…
en.body:
The New Non-Resident Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the Kingdom of Bhutan, His Excellency Ibrahim Shaheeb, presented his Letter of Credence to the King of Bhutan, His Majesty Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, at a ceremony held in the Grand Kuenray at Tashichhodzong, this morning.

On presenting the credentials His Majesty King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, congratulated Ambassador Shaheeb and expressed confidence that the Ambassador will work to reinforce the close ties between the Maldives and Bhutan. At the brief audience with His Majesty, Ambassador Shaheeb mentioned that it was a privilege to have had the opportunity to work towards the mutual benefit of the two countries. Ambassador also assured the commitment to work closely in order to further elevate the existing cordial partnership.

Ambassador Shaheeb extended the warmest greeting and sincere good wishes from the President of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, on behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives to His Majesty the King of Bhutan. As the newly accredited Ambassador, Ibrahim Shaheeb assured his commitment to work closely with the Government of Bhutan to further strengthen the close relations between Maldives and Bhutan during his tenure.

Following the presentation ceremony, the newly accredited Ambassador of Maldives to the Kingdom of Bhutan will pay a courtesy call to the Prime Minister, His Excellency Dr. Lotay Tshering and Minister of Foreign Affairs and External Trade of Bhutan, His Excellency Dr. Tandi Dorji, at separate events. Ambassador Shaheeb will also hold meetings with senior government officials in Bhutan.

Ambassador Shaheeb is accompanied by First Secretary at the High Commission of Maldives in India, Mr. Mohamed Najeel.

en.title: Maldives and European Union sign the Financing Agreement to launch the initiative on strengthening the rule of law and anti-corruption in the Maldives
en.description: The Maldives and European Union officially launched a new flagship initiative to strengthen the rule of law and anti-corruption in the Maldives, at the sidelines of the 4th Maldives EU Senior Officials Meeting in…
en.body:
The Maldives and European Union officially launched a new flagship initiative to strengthen the rule of law and anti-corruption in the Maldives, at the sidelines of the 4th Maldives EU Senior Officials Meeting in Brussels today. This five year programme, funded by the European Union for a total amount of EUR 5 million (MVR 83 million), is based on the Maldives’ priority needs and reforms, and will be implemented in close partnership with all relevant actors from the justice and anti-corruption sectors.

The Agreement was signed by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel for the Government of Maldives, and Director for Asia, Middle East and the Pacific, Directorate General for International Partnerships Mr. Peteris Ustubs for the European Union.

The ’Strengthening the Rule of Law and Anti-Corruption’ programme will build upon and complement the achievements and lessons learnt from past EU initiatives in the sector. Its main objective is to strengthen the rule of law and reduce corruption in the Maldives, through: (1) supporting the country in developing an effective, accountable and inclusive justice system, and; (2) strengthening anti-corruption efforts through better legal frameworks, institutional capacity building and improving public perception.

en.title: The European Union and the Maldives hold the 4th Senior Officials Meeting
en.description: The Fourth Senior Officials Meeting between the European Union (EU) and the Maldives was held in Brussels on 13 June 2023.
en.body:
The Fourth Senior Officials Meeting between the European Union (EU) and the Maldives was held in Brussels on 13 June 2023.

The meeting re-affirmed the strong bilateral ties between the EU and the Maldives as the partners celebrate the 40th anniversary of establishing diplomatic relations. The EU and the Maldives confirmed their mutual interest to further strengthen and deepen the mutually beneficial cooperation rooted in shared values and commitment to the principles of the UN Charter and international law.

The EU congratulated the Maldives on its accession to the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS) and welcomed the country among the signatories of the new EU-OACPS Agreement, which will further enhance the EU-Maldives partnership as well as regional integration. The Maldives and the EU discussed how the accession to the new EU-OACPS agreement should provide a pathway for the Maldives to negotiate accession to the OACPS’ Eastern and Southern African Group’s interim Economic Partnership Agreement with the EU, which provides for a tariff-free access to the EU market, including for tuna products. The EU and the Maldives discussed the concrete steps in the coming months towards this end.

The EU and the Maldives also discussed further deepening their engagement through the implementation of the EU Strategy for cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. The EU expressed appreciation to Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid for his important contribution as a moderator and rapporteur for the Roundtable on Green Opportunities and Overcoming Global Challenges in the EU Indo-Pacific Ministerial Forum held in Stockholm on 13 May 2023.

The EU stressed the importance of maintaining a continuous commitment towards the consolidation of democracy, the protection of human rights, the strengthening of the rule of law, and the fight against corruption, based on implementing reforms in the justice sector. In this regard, the EU re-affirmed its ongoing support to the Maldives’ efforts in consolidating democratic reforms and its implementation. The EU and the Maldives underlined the importance attached to the vibrant civil society, and freedom of expression and opinion as key foundations of democracy, essential to uphold in particular as the Maldives prepares for Presidential elections in September.

The EU and the Maldives agreed to continue close cooperation in the UN and all relevant multilateral fora to address global challenges such as peace and security, sustainable development, climate change and biodiversity loss, water and plastic pollution. Likewise, they reaffirmed their commitment to work closely together on promoting human rights in multilateral fora, including through the Human Rights Council.

The EU and the Maldives discussed EU support under the 2021-2027 Multiannual Indicative Programme (MIP) focusing on some of the Maldives’ key development priorities such as green transition, climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity protection and circular economy. The EU also reaffirmed its commitment to support good governance, judiciary reforms and security. As an important step into this direction, during this Senior Officials Meeting, the EU and the Maldives signed the Financing Agreement of the new €5 million action providing support to enhance the rule of law and to reduce corruption in the Maldives.

The EU and the Maldives explored avenues to further enhance security cooperation, especially in areas of counterterrorism and preventing violent extremism, as well as in maritime security domain.

As partners in trade and investment, the EU and Maldives will continue expanding their economic cooperation. The Maldives and the EU will explore synergies to adapt their Business Roundtable to the new context provided by the OACPS adhesion, to attract European investors and investments to the Maldives.

The EU and the Maldives are committed to the global fight against illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing and will continue their strong bilateral cooperation in this domain. During the meeting, they discussed the need for better cooperation and coordination to ensure sustainable management of fish stocks through the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission.

The EU and the Maldives welcomed the agreement on a UNCLOS implementing agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction or “Treaty of the High Seas” and are committed to its swift ratification and implementation.

The EU and the Maldives discussed Maldives’ request to grant visa free travel for Maldivian nationals to EU Member States. The Maldives’ request for visa-free travel would be addressed when the next review of visa lists takes place. The discussion reflected the ongoing efforts to strengthen relations and promote greater connectivity between the EU and Maldives.

The Fourth Senior Officials Meeting was co-chaired by Paola Pampaloni, Deputy Managing Director for Asia and Pacific at the European External Action Service, and Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Kazakhstan
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of condolence to H.E. Murat Nurtleu, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan, following the tragic fire that occurred in the…
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of condolence to H.E. Murat Nurtleu, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan, following the tragic fire that occurred in the Abai region of Kazakhstan.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“I was deeply shocked and saddened to hear the tragic news of the devastating forest fires in the Abai region of Kazakhstan.

The Government and the people of the Maldives join me in conveying our profound sympathies and condolences to the families who lost their loved ones and those impacted by this tragic incident.

Our thoughts and prayers are with the victims, and all affected by the tragedy, and we wish for the quick recovery of the injured.“

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid pays a courtesy call on the President of Seychelles

en.body:

At the meeting held at Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi, Minister Shahid welcomed the President and his delegation to the Maldives and reaffirmed the strong commitment of the Government of Maldives to further enhance bilateral cooperation and increase collaboration at the regional and international levels on matters of mutual interest.

Minister Shahid further noted that the agreements signed today, will be mutually beneficial to both, the people of Maldives and the people Seychelles and expressed hope that the Visa Exemption Agreement will allow greater people-to-people interaction between both countries. Minister Shahid also reaffirmed that the Maldives stands ready to implement the outcomes agreed upon by the two leaders during the Official Talks held in the morning at the President’s Office.

President Wavel Ramkalawan is currently on a State Visit to the Maldives from 11 – 14 June 2023 on the invitation of the President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. President Ramkalawan is accompanied by Her Excellency Linda Ramkalawan, First Lady of the Republic of Seychelles and a high-level delegation from the Government of Seychelles, including His Excellency Sylvestre Radegonde, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Tourism.

en.title: Maldives and The Gambia Sign a Visa Waiver Agreement
en.description: The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of The Gambia today signed the Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements, which allows for the exemption of visas for single or…
en.body:
The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Republic of The Gambia today signed the Agreement on Mutual Exemption of Visa Requirements, which allows for the exemption of visas for single or multiple entry, exit or transit for both countries' nationals, for a period of 30 days.

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Government of Maldives by His Excellency Mohamed Khaleel, Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and on behalf of the Government of The Gambia by His Excellency Mr Omar Gibril Sallah, Ambassador of The Gambia to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The signing ceremony was held at the Embassy of the Maldives in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

During the discussions following the signing ceremony, Ambassador Mohamed Khaleel expressed his gratitude to the Government of The Gambia for its commitment towards enhancing the existing ties of friendship and cooperation between the two countries and conveyed hope that the signing of this agreement will increase avenues for further engagement and people-to-people contact between the Maldives and The Gambia. Ambassador Salla conveyed the Government of The Gambia's commitment to work with the Maldives on areas of mutual interest, to further strengthen relationship between the two countries.

en.title: Maldives delegation departs for 4th Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union
en.description: The Maldives delegation attending the Fourth Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union departs to Brussels, Belgium, today.
en.body:
The Maldives delegation attending the Fourth Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union departs to Brussels, Belgium, today.

The annual Senior Officials Meeting serves as a platform for fostering transparent and positive interaction between the Maldives and the European Union, strengthening the existing bonds of friendship and collaboration. This year marks the fourth edition of the meeting, scheduled to take place on June 13, 2023, in Brussels, Belgium. The third Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union was held on 25 October 2022, in Male’.

The agenda for this year's meeting includes discussions on various topics such as developments in the EU and the Maldives, the Post-Cotonou Agreement, governance, democracy, human rights, rule of law, prevention of violent extremism and counterterrorism, economic and trade cooperation, environment and climate change, development cooperation, fisheries, Schengen Visa facilitation, cooperation in the UN, regional developments, and maritime security.

The Maldives delegation will be led by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel. Senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the President’s Office, Ministry of Economic Development, Ministry of Fisheries, Marine Resources and Agriculture, Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, Maldives Police Service and National Counter Terrorism Centre will also be in attendance.

The delegation from the European Union will be led by the Deputy Managing Director at the European External Action Service, Paola Pampaloni.

During this visit, the Maldives delegation will also meet with the Secretary-General of Organization of the African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS), His Excellency Georges Rebelo Chikoti; Managing Director for Asia and Pacific at the European External Action Service (EEAS), Mr. Gunnar Wiegand; Director-General at the Directorate-General Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (MARE), Mrs. Charline Vitcheva; EU Counter-Terrorism Coordinator, Mr. Ilkka Salmi; Deputy Director-General at the Directorate-General International Partnerships (INTPA), Mrs. Myriam Ferran; and Director-General at the Directorate-General Trade (TRADE), Mrs. Sabine Weyand.

en.title: Meeting of the Senior Officials of the Fourth Session of the Maldives – Sri Lanka Joint Commission
en.description: The Meeting of the Senior Officials of the Fourth Session of the Maldives – Sri Lanka Joint Commission was held on 6 June 2023, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka. The Meeting was Co-Chaired by Her…
en.body:
The Meeting of the Senior Officials of the Fourth Session of the Maldives – Sri Lanka Joint Commission was held on 6 June 2023, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka. The Meeting was Co-Chaired by Her Excellency Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary, Bilateral at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, and Her Excellency Ms. Yasoja Gunasekera, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka.

During the discussions, the two sides deliberated on several bilateral issues of importance to both countries, including trade & investment, defense, tourism, fisheries, education, health, employment, youth, sports and skill development, consular and cultural affairs. Discussions also focused on consular issues and regional and international cooperation.

The Maldives delegation comprised of delegates from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Arts, Culture, and Heritage, Ministry of Fisheries, Marine Resources and Agriculture, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Higher Education, Ministry of Economic Development and the Ministry of Youth, Sports and Community Empowerment.

Interventions were made by His Excellency Dr. Abdulla Rasheed Ahmed, Minister of State for Education, His Excellency Dr. Ahmed Salih, Minister of State for Tourism, His Excellency Ali Nazeer, Minister of State for Home Affairs, Mr. Shamau Shareef, Deputy Minister of the Ministry of Health, Mr. Shamun Hameed, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Arts, Culture, and Heritage, Mr. Adam Ziyad, Director General of the Ministry of Fisheries, Marine Resources and Agriculture, Lieutenant Colonel Ismail Athif, Principal Director, at the Ministry of Defence, Ms. Sonath Abdul Sattar, Senior Policy Director at the Ministry of Higher Education, Mr. Ahmed Ifthikhaar, Director at the Ministry of Economic Development and Ms. Zubaidha Abdul Hameed, Deputy Director at the Ministry of Youth, Sports and Community Empowerment.

The Ministerial segment of the Fourth Session of the Maldives - Sri Lanka Joint Commission was held today, 7 June 2023 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka. The Maldives delegation was led by the His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and the Sri Lankan delegation was led by His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry.

en.title: Maldives and Sri Lanka sign three Agreements during Official Visit
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka, His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry today witnessed the signing of three agreements between the…
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka, His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry today witnessed the signing of three agreements between the Maldives and Sri Lanka. The agreements were signed during the Fourth Session of the Maldives – Sri Lanka Joint Commission held today at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka.

The agreements that were signed today include the “Memorandum of Understanding between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka on the Establishment of the Maldives Cultural Centre in Sri Lanka”. The agreement was signed on behalf of the Maldivian Government by His Excellency Ali Faiz, High Commissioner of Maldives to Sri Lanka and His Excellency Somarathne Vidanapathirana, Secretary to the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs of Sri Lanka.

The “Memorandum of Understanding between the Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka on the Field of Health Cooperation” was signed by Mr. Shamau Shareef, Deputy Minister of Ministry of Health on behalf of the Government of Maldives and His Excellency Dr. A.K. Sunil Bernard De Alwis, Additional Secretary (Medical Services) to the Ministry of Health of Sri Lanka.

His Excellency Mohamed Thoriq, Minister of State for Arts, Culture and Heritage, signed on behalf of the Maldivian Government, the “Memorandum of Understanding on Cultural Cooperation between the Government of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the Government of the Republic of Maldives”. The MoU was signed on behalf of the Sri Lankan Government by His Excellency Somarathne Vidanapathirana, Secretary to the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs of Sri Lanka.

The agreements aim to foster greater bilateral relations and cooperation between the Maldives and Sri Lanka in the field of cultural and health cooperation and people-to-people relations.

en.title: Minister Shahid arrives in Sri Lanka on an Official Visit
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has arrived in Colombo on an Official Visit.
en.body:

Minister Shahid will lead the Maldives delegation at the Fourth Session of the Maldives – Sri Lanka Joint Commission, which will be held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka, today, 7 June 2023. During this visit Minister Shahid will pay courtesy calls on His Excellency Ranil Wickremesinghe, President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka, His Excellency Dinesh Gunawardena, Prime Minister of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and meet his counterpart, Foreign Minister M.U.M Ali Sabry.

Minister Shahid is accompanied by His Excellency Ahmed Latheef, Foreign Secretary, His Excellency Dr Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary, Economic Development, Her Excellency, Dr Hala Hameed, Secretary, Bilateral, and Ms. Aishath Fareena, Assistant Director, Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

en.body:
The Fourth Session of the Maldives – Sri Lanka Joint Commission was held this afternoon at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka. His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives led the Maldivian delegation and His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka led the Sri Lankan delegation.

During the Meeting, the Foreign Ministers deliberated on a wide range of issues of mutual importance to both countries. In particular, the discussions were focused on fostering greater cooperation in the economic, educational, health, defence and cultural fields, among others. The MoU on Health Cooperation was signed by Deputy Minister of Health Mr. Shamau Shareef, on behalf of the Government of Maldives and His Excellency Dr. A.K. Sunil Bernard De Alwis, Additional Secretary (Medical Services) to the Ministry of Health of Sri Lanka.

The MoU on Cultural Cooperation was signed by Minister of State for Arts, Culture and Heritage His Excellency Mohamed Thoriq, on behalf of the Government of Maldives and His Excellency Somarathne Vidanapathirana, Secretary to the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs of Sri Lanka.

Her Excellency Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary, Bilateral led the Maldivian delegation and Her Excellency Yasoja Gunasekera, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Sri Lanka led the Sri Lankan delegation at the Senior Officials’ Meeting.
